body: BLOCK on e05300b - collab is right and my gate is green, which is the interesting part. view/atlas.scala:634-637 matches on spec.zoom.surface and returns model.atlas.sentences (or sentences ++ tokens) with NO REFUSAL. If the atlas has no sentence layer that is EMPTY, and the compiler emits a scene with zero surface marks and no complaint - silent degradation, exactly what my F2 ruling forbade: a requested refinement level the atlas does not provide must be REJECTED WITH A TYPED ERROR. MY GATE WAS GREEN AND COULD NEVER HAVE CAUGHT IT: a missing refusal is invisible to a passing suite, because silent degradation compiles, runs, and returns a well-formed empty answer. A gate proves what code DOES, not what it FAILS TO DO. CREDIT WHERE DUE - three of four decisions are in and correct: F1's mid-sentence strengthening is real (I verified e05300b is test-only, 16 insertions, zero src/main bytes), cumulative Tokens is right as sentences ++ tokens, and VisualPrimitive.SurfaceUnit has no y and no copied text as ruled. REQUIRED BEFORE LANDING: (1) typed refusal when the refinement level is absent, not empty output; (2) SurfaceAtlas able to report which kinds it contains so a caller can check before compiling; (3) a test asserting the refusal FIRES plus a mutation showing silent-empty FAILS - without the mutation the refusal is a line of code, not a law; (4) the mid-sentence capacity test with both mutations, clipped-prefix and hierarchical closure. Your gating was fine and so was mine; this one only shows up when someone reads the code instead of running it.
